description: Exercises draft-pidlisnyi-aps-03 section 2.4's requirement that a resolver select the key version authorized at a delegation's issued_at, not the key current at verification time, and its second paragraph's requirement that a before-boundary issued_at claim for a retired key is only accepted with boundary_evidence corroborating it. Same identifier and verification_method throughout; K1 is authorized for issued_at before rotation_boundary and only with boundary_evidence, K2 for issued_at at or after it unconditionally. Every vector is verified at now, which is after rotation_boundary, so every vector exercises resolution across the rotation, not resolution before it happened.

historical.name: historical-key-resolution
historical.description: Resolves the key authorized at the delegation's own issued_at against rotation_boundary, and for a before-boundary claim additionally requires boundary_evidence. This is the correct draft-03 section 2.4 behavior and is the fixture's positive control.

current_key_only.name: current-key-only
current_key_only.description: Negative control. Ignores issued_at and always resolves to the key that is current at verification time (K2, since every vector here is verified after rotation_boundary). This is exactly the insufficient behavior draft-03 section 2.4 names: 'selecting the key that is current at verification time is insufficient.' It fails every vector whose correct key is K1, the retired key: KRH-01 and KRH-04 on the accept/reject pair, and KRH-05 because resolving K2 against a K1 signature reports invalid, not the indeterminate this policy's own evidence blindness would otherwise still owe it.

claim_trusting.name: claim-trusting
claim_trusting.description: Negative control. Selects K1 or K2 from the issued_at claim alone, exactly like historical-key-resolution's before/after split, but never consults boundary_evidence. This is what this fixture's own resolver used to do before this correction, and it is exactly the gap draft-03 section 2.4's second paragraph identifies: it treats an issuer's unverified issued_at claim as sufficient on its own to authorize the retired key. It matches historical-key-resolution on every vector except KRH-05, the one vector whose correct result depends on evidence this resolver never looks at.

cases.description: issued_at before rotation_boundary, signed with K1, boundary_evidence present and corroborating. K1 is the key authorized at issued_at, and evidence establishes the claim is honest, so this is valid. A verifier that instead resolves the key current at verification time (K2) fails this vector, which is what current-key-only does.
issued_at after rotation_boundary, signed with K2. K2 is the key authorized at issued_at, unconditionally: K2's validity window does not close, so no boundary_evidence question arises for it. Valid.

issued_at after rotation_boundary, but the signature was actually produced with K1, the retired key. A resolver correctly picks K2 for this issued_at (K2 needs no boundary_evidence), so K2's public key is checked against a signature K1 produced, and the signature check fails. K1 is not authorized at this issued_at.

issued_at before rotation_boundary, boundary_evidence present (the same claimed issued_at as KRH-01, corroborated the same way), but the signature was actually produced with K2, a key not yet authorized then. A resolver correctly picks K1 for this issued_at, so K1's public key is checked against a signature K2 produced, and the signature check fails. This isolates the reject on the signing key alone: the only stated change from KRH-01 is which key signed it, not the evidence.

issued_at before rotation_boundary, signed with K1: the same key/time relationship as KRH-01. boundary_evidence is absent. Per draft-03 section 2.4's second paragraph, issued_at is only an issuer claim, and without a timestamp, transparency-log, or equivalent evidence source establishing that signing fell before the boundary, the key-authority result is indeterminate, even though the signature is cryptographically valid. KRH-05's issued_at differs from KRH-01's only because the resolver is called with (issuer, verification_method, issued_at) and nothing else, so two records claiming the identical triple could not be given different results by any resolver; the size of that difference carries no significance of its own. This is the same input class as KRH-01, not a distinct boundary-adjacency test.
